learn.title: Branches
learn.body: In a parallel circuit each part sits on its own branch, so the current has several paths. Every branch has the same voltage as the source. If one branch breaks, the others keep working.

learn.title: Currents add
learn.body: The branch currents add up: $I_{total}=I_1+I_2$. More paths means more current, so the total resistance goes down: $\frac{1}{R_{total}}=\frac{1}{R_1}+\frac{1}{R_2}$. It is always smaller than the smallest branch.

learn.title: Two branches
learn.body: 6 ohms and 3 ohms are in parallel across 12 V.
Two equal resistors in parallel give half of one. Two 10 ohm resistors give 5 ohms.

questions.prompt: 4 ohms and 12 ohms are in parallel. What is the total in ohms?

questions.explanation: The other branches still have a complete path and the full voltage.

questions.prompt: Branch currents are 2 A and 3 A. What is the total current in A?
